SmartScreen:ShellConfigureSmartScreen,Configure Windows Defender SmartScreen,Windows Components > Windows Defender SmartScreen > Explorer,Machine,88,90,81,Disabled,Enabled,Disabled,Windows 11 24H2 - Computer: Enabled; Pick one of the following settings = Warn and prevent bypass,"This policy allows you to turn Windows Defender SmartScreen on or off. If you disable or do not configure this setting, you will not join Microsoft MAPS.

In Windows 10, Basic membership is no longer available, so setting the value to 1 or 2 enrolls the device into Advanced membership."

WindowsDefender:RealtimeProtection_PerformanceModeStatus,Configure performance mode status,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Real-time Protection,Machine,12,79,39,—,Disabled,,,"This policy controls Microsoft Defender Antivirus performance mode for Dev Drives.

A Dev Drive is a disk drive optimized for higher performance in software development scenarios. When this policy is Enabled or not configured, Performance mode is turned on for Microsoft Defender Antivirus. In Performance mode, Microsoft Defender Antivirus security checks of content stored on Dev Drives are conducted asynchronously to enhance performance. Performance mode requires the following policies also be enabled: “Enable dev drive”, and “Dev drive filter attach policy”.

If you either Enable or do not configure this policy setting, Performance mode is turned on.

If you Disable this policy setting, Performance mode is turned off and Microsoft Defender Antivirus will protect a Dev Drive in the same way as other drives."
WindowsDefender:RealtimeProtection_RealtimeScanDirection,Configure monitoring for incoming and outgoing file and program activity,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Real-time Protection,Machine,10,22,38,—,—,,Windows 11 24H2 - Defender Antivirus: Enabled; Configure monitoring for incoming and outgoing file and program activity = bi-directional (full on-access),"This policy setting allows you to configure monitoring for incoming and outgoing files, without having to turn off monitoring entirely. It is recommended for use on servers where there is a lot of incoming and outgoing file activity but for performance reasons need to have scanning disabled for a particular scan direction. The appropriate configuration should be evaluated based on the server role.

Note that this configuration is only honored for NTFS volumes. For any other file system type, full monitoring of file and program activity will be present on those volumes.

The options for this setting are mutually exclusive:
0 = Scan incoming and outgoing files (default)
1 = Scan incoming files only
2 = Scan outgoing files only

Any other value, or if the value does not exist, resolves to the default (0).

If you enable this setting, the specified type of monitoring will be enabled.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, monitoring for incoming and outgoing files will be enabled."
WindowsDefender:Remediation_BNB_BFP_BruteForceProtectionExclusions,Set exclusions from Brute-Force Protection,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Remediation > Behavioral Network Blocks > Brute-Force Protection,Machine,15,70,25,—,Enabled,,,"Specify IP addresses, subnets or workstation names to exclude from Brute-Force Protection. WindowsDefender:Remediation_BNB_BFP_BruteForceProtection_Aggressiveness,Configure Brute-Force Protection aggressiveness,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Remediation > Behavioral Network Blocks > Brute-Force Protection,Machine,69,84,27,Disabled,Enabled,,,"Set the criteria for when Brute-Force Protection blocks IP addresses.

WindowsDefender:Remediation_BNB_BFP_BruteForceProtection_ConfiguredState,Configure Remote Encryption Protection Mode,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Remediation > Behavioral Network Blocks > Brute-Force Protection,Machine,32,80,32,—,Enabled,,,"Set the mode for Brute-Force Protection in Microsoft Defender Antivirus, which can detect and block attempts to forcibly initiate sign in and initiate sessions.

WindowsDefender:Remediation_BNB_REP_RemoteEncryptionProtection_Aggressiveness,Configure how aggressively Remote Encryption Protection blocks threats,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Remediation > Behavioral Network Blocks > Remote Encryption Protection,Machine,60,85,39,Disabled,Enabled,,,"Set the criteria for when remote encryption preventionprotection blocks IP addresses.

WindowsDefender:Remediation_BNB_REP_RemoteEncryptionProtection_MaxBlockTime,Configure Remote Encryption Protection blocking time,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Remediation > Behavioral Network Blocks > Remote Encryption Protection,Machine,14,66,29,—,Enabled,,,"Set the maximum time an IP address is blocked by Remote Encryption Protection. WindowsDefender:Remediation_LocalSettingOverrideScan_ScheduleTime,Configure local setting override for the time of day to run a scheduled full scan to complete remediation,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Remediation,Machine,9,43,30,—,—,,,"This policy setting configures a local override for the configuration of the time to run a scheduled full scan to complete remediation. WindowsDefender:Remediation_Scan_ScheduleDay,Specify the day of the week to run a scheduled full scan to complete remediation,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Remediation,Machine,14,46,23,—,—,,,"This policy setting allows you to specify the day of the week on which to perform a scheduled full scan in order to complete remediation. WindowsDefender:Remediation_Scan_ScheduleTime,Specify the time of day to run a scheduled full scan to complete remediation,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Remediation,Machine,9,24,28,—,—,,,"This policy setting allows you to specify the time of day at which to perform a scheduled full scan in order to complete remediation. WindowsDefender:Reporting_ServiceHealthReportInterval,Configure time interval for service health reports,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Reporting,Machine,82,24,7,Disabled,—,,,"This policy setting configures the time interval (in minutes) for the service health reports to be sent from endpoints.

WindowsDefender:Root_EngineUpdateChannel,Select the channel for Microsoft Defender monthly engine updates,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus,Machine,28,37,30,—,—,,,"Enable this policy to specify when devices receive Microsoft Defender engine updates during the monthly gradual rollout.​

Beta Channel: Devices set to this channel will be the first to receive new updates. Select Beta Channel to participate in identifying and reporting issues to Microsoft. Devices in the Windows Insider Program are subscribed to this channel by default. For use in (manual) test environments only and a limited number of devices.
Current Channel (Preview): Devices set to this channel will be offered updates earliest during the monthly gradual release cycle. Suggested for pre-production/validation environments.
Current Channel (Staged): Devices will be offered updates after the monthly gradual release cycle. Suggested to apply to a small, representative part of your production population (~10%).
Current Channel (Broad): Devices will be offered updates only after the gradual release cycle completes. Suggested to apply to a broad set of devices in your production population (~10-100%).
Critical - Time delay: Devices will be offered updates with a 48-hour delay. Suggested for critical environments only.

If you disable or do not configure this policy, the device will stay up to date automatically during the gradual release cycle. Suitable for most devices."
WindowsDefender:Root_PUAProtection,Configure detection for potentially unwanted applications,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus,Machine,21,90,64,—,Enabled,,Windows 11 24H2 - Defender Antivirus: Enabled; Configure detection for potentially unwanted applications = Block,"Enable or disable detection for potentially unwanted applications. You can choose to block, audit, or allow when potentially unwanted software is being downloaded or attempts to install itself on your computer.

Enabled:

-Block: Potentially unwanted software will be blocked.
-Audit Mode: Potentially unwanted software will not be blocked, however if this feature would have blocked access if it were set to Block, then a record of the event will be in the event logs.

Disabled:

Not configured:
Same as Disabled."

WindowsDefender:Root_SecurityIntelligenceUpdateChannel,Select the channel for Microsoft Defender daily security intelligence updates,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus,Machine,23,31,34,—,—,,,"Enable this policy to specify when devices receive Microsoft Defender security intelligence updates during the daily gradual rollout.

WindowsDefender:Scan_AllowPause,Allow users to pause scan,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,8,73,79,—,Disabled,,,"This policy setting allows you to manage whether or not end users can pause a scan in progress.

If you disable this setting, users will not be able to pause scans."
WindowsDefender:Scan_ArchiveMaxDepth,Specify the maximum depth to scan archive files,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,10,60,18,—,Enabled,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure the maximum directory depth level into which archive files such as .ZIP or .CAB are unpacked during scanning. The default directory depth level is 0.

If you enable this setting, archive files will be scanned to the directory depth level specified.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, archive files will be scanned to the default directory depth level."
WindowsDefender:Scan_ArchiveMaxSize,Specify the maximum size of archive files to be scanned,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,13,45,22,—,—,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure the maximum size of archive files such as .ZIP or .CAB that will be scanned. The value represents file size in kilobytes (KB). The default value is 0 and represents no limit to archive size for scanning.

If you enable this setting, archive files less than or equal to the size specified will be scanned.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, archive files will be scanned according to the default value."
WindowsDefender:Scan_AvgCPULoadFactor,Specify the maximum percentage of CPU utilization during a scan,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,4,11,43,—,—,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure the maximum percentage CPU utilization permitted during a scan. Valid values for this setting are a percentage represented by the integers 5 to 100. A value of 0 indicates that there should be no throttling of CPU utilization. The default value is 50.

If you enable this setting, CPU utilization will not exceed the percentage specified.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, CPU utilization will not exceed the default value."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DaysUntilAggressiveCatchupQuickScan,Trigger a quick scan after X days without any scans,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,20,74,29,—,Enabled,,,"This policy setting defines the number of days that can pass since the last scan before an aggresive catchup quick scan is automatically triggered. The value represents the number of days that can pass without any scans being performed before an agressive quick scan will be triggered.

Valid values range from 7 to 60 days. If not configured, aggressive quick scans will be disabled. By default, the value is set to 25 days when enabled."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisableArchiveScanning,Scan archive files,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,15,35,19,—,—,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure scans for malicious software and unwanted software in archive files such as .ZIP or .CAB files.

If you enable or do not configure this setting, archive files will be scanned.

If you disable this setting, archive files will not be scanned. However, archives are always scanned during directed scans."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisableCatchupFullScan,Turn on catch-up full scan,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,11,65,24,—,Enabled,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure catch-up scans for scheduled full scans. A catch-up scan is a scan that is initiated because a regularly scheduled scan was missed. Usually these scheduled scans are missed because the computer was turned off at the scheduled time.

If you enable this setting, catch-up scans for scheduled full scans will be turned on. If a computer is offline for two consecutive scheduled scans, a catch-up scan is started the next time someone logs on to the computer. If there is no scheduled scan configured, there will be no catch-up scan run.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, catch-up scans for scheduled full scans will be turned off."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisableCatchupQuickScan,Turn on catch-up quick scan,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,13,60,24,—,Enabled,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure catch-up scans for scheduled quick scans. A catch-up scan is a scan that is initiated because a regularly scheduled scan was missed. Usually these scheduled scans are missed because the computer was turned off at the scheduled time.

If you enable this setting, catch-up scans for scheduled quick scans will be turned on. If a computer is offline for two consecutive scheduled scans, a catch-up scan is started the next time someone logs on to the computer. If there is no scheduled scan configured, there will be no catch-up scan run.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, catch-up scans for scheduled quick scans will be turned off."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisableEmailScanning,Turn on e-mail scanning,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,23,66,20,—,Enabled,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure e-mail scanning. When e-mail scanning is enabled, the engine will parse the mailbox and mail files, according to their specific format, in order to analyze the mail bodies and attachments. Several e-mail formats are currently supported, for example: pst (Outlook), dbx, mbx, mime (Outlook Express), binhex (Mac). Email scanning is not supported on modern email clients.

If you enable this setting, e-mail scanning will be enabled.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, e-mail scanning will be disabled."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisableHeuristics,Turn on heuristics,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,14,52,30,—,Enabled,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure heuristics. Suspicious detections will be suppressed right before reporting to the engine client. Turning off heuristics will reduce the capability to flag new threats. It is recommended that you do not turn off heuristics.

If you enable or do not configure this setting, heuristics will be enabled.

If you disable this setting, heuristics will be disabled."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisablePackedExeScanning,Scan packed executables,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,11,49,18,—,—,,Windows 11 24H2 - Defender Antivirus: Enabled,"This policy setting allows you to configure scanning for packed executables. It is recommended that this type of scanning remain enabled.

If you disable this setting, packed executables will not be scanned."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisableRemovableDriveScanning,Scan removable drives,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,18,84,26,—,Enabled,,Windows 11 24H2 - Defender Antivirus: Enabled,"This policy setting allows you to manage whether or not to scan for malicious software and unwanted software in the contents of removable drives, such as USB flash drives, when running a full scan.

If you enable this setting, removable drives will be scanned during any type of scan.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, removable drives will not be scanned during a full scan. Removable drives may still be scanned during quick scan and custom scan."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisableReparsePointScanning,Turn on reparse point scanning,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,7,26,11,—,—,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure reparse point scanning. If you allow reparse points to be scanned, there is a possible risk of recursion. However, the engine supports following reparse points to a maximum depth so at worst scanning could be slowed. Reparse point scanning is disabled by default and this is the recommended state for this functionality.

If you enable this setting, reparse point scanning will be enabled.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, reparse point scanning will be disabled."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisableRestorePoint,Create a system restore point,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,11,32,31,—,—,,,"This policy setting allows you to create a system restore point on the computer on a daily basis prior to cleaning.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, a system restore point will not be created."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisableScanningMappedNetworkDrivesForFullScan,Run full scan on mapped network drives,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,15,76,23,—,Enabled,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure scanning mapped network drives.

If you enable this setting, mapped network drives will be scanned.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, mapped network drives will not be scanned."
WindowsDefender:Scan_DisableScanningNetworkFiles,Configure scanning of network files,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,14,46,37,—,—,,,"This policy setting allows the scanning of network files using on access protection. WindowsDefender:Scan_LocalSettingOverrideAvgCPULoadFactor,Configure local setting override for maximum percentage of CPU utilization,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,6,28,28,—,—,,,"This policy setting configures a local override for the configuration of maximum percentage of CPU utilization during scan. WindowsDefender:Scan_LowCpuPriority,Configure low CPU priority for scheduled scans,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,5,8,23,—,—,,,"This policy setting allows you to enable or disable low CPU priority for scheduled scans.

WindowsDefender:Scan_MissedScheduledScanCountBeforeCatchup,Define the number of days after which a catch-up scan is forced,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,11,51,28,—,Enabled,,,"This policy setting allows you to define the number of consecutive scheduled scans that can be missed after which a catch-up scan will be forced. WindowsDefender:Scan_PurgeItemsAfterDelay,Turn on removal of items from scan history folder,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Scan,Machine,74,24,22,Enabled,—,,,"This policy setting defines the number of days items should be kept in the scan history folder before being permanently removed. WindowsDefender:ServiceKeepAlive,Allow antimalware service to remain running always,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus,Machine,18,69,44,—,Enabled,,,"This policy setting allows you to configure whether or not the antimalware service remains running when antivirus and antispyware security intelligence is disabled. WindowsDefender:SpynetReporting,Join Microsoft MAPS,Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > MAPS,Machine,33,35,16,—,—,Enabled; Join Microsoft MAPS = Disabled,Windows 11 24H2 - Defender Antivirus: Enabled; Join Microsoft MAPS = Advanced MAPS,"This policy setting allows you to join Microsoft MAPS. Microsoft MAPS is the online community that helps you choose how to respond to potential threats. The community also helps stop the spread of new malicious software infections.

You can choose to send basic or additional information about detected software. Additional information helps Microsoft create new security intelligence and help it to protect your computer. This information can include things like location of detected items on your computer if harmful software was removed. The information will be automatically collected and sent. In some instances, personal information might unintentionally be sent to Microsoft. However, Microsoft will not use this information to identify you or contact you.

Possible options are:
(0x0) Disabled (default)
(0x1) Basic membership
(0x2) Advanced membership

Basic membership will send basic information to Microsoft about software that has been detected, including where the software came from, the actions that you apply or that are applied automatically, and whether the actions were successful.

Advanced membership, in addition to basic information, will send more information to Microsoft about malicious software, spyware, and potentially unwanted software, including the location of the software, file names, how the software operates, and how it has impacted your computer.

If you enable this setting, you will join Microsoft MAPS with the membership specified.

If you disable or do not configure this setting, you will not join Microsoft MAPS.

In Windows 10, Basic membership is no longer available, so setting the value to 1 or 2 enrolls the device into Advanced membership."
